title.purpose: Note card titles and section headings. Bricolage Grotesque, tight negative tracking, optical sizing on.

body.purpose: Note excerpts, checklist rows, all running text. Work Sans.

label.purpose: Tag chips, media kind badges, relative time, eyebrows. Uppercase, wide tracking, never below 11px.

shadows.name: rest-day
shadows.purpose: Every card and raised surface at rest in the day theme.

shadows.name: hover-day
shadows.purpose: Card hover and FAB in the day theme.

shadows.name: rest-night
shadows.purpose: Card rest in the night theme, always paired with the identity glow.

shadows.name: hover-night
shadows.purpose: Card hover in the night theme, paired with the intensified glow.

shadows.name: glow-rest
shadows.purpose: Night-only. The card's identity colour as emitted light. Carries depth where shadow cannot.

shadows.name: glow-pinned
shadows.purpose: Night-only pinned state, with the border at full identity colour.

motion.name: spring-feather
motion.purpose: The default card spring. Damping ratio ~1.34, so it is overdamped and never overshoots. Measured: 84px of travel with 0px overshoot.

motion.name: reflow-ease
motion.purpose: Intended easing for the wall re-packing after a pin. NOTE: currently only applied in Rows packing; the packed-column feed animates x/y directly and falls back to Motion's default spring.

motion.name: hover-scale-card
motion.purpose: Applied to the card's surface layer only, never the layer holding text.

motion.name: hover-scale-button
motion.purpose: Icon buttons, always paired with a material change so reduced motion retains the affordance.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Hard killswitch outranking every world stylesheet. Every hover that used scale must still change material.

motion.name: layout-switch
motion.value: same placement path, animated x/y/width targets
motion.purpose: Masonry <-> Stack. Cards travel to their new slot and change width; must interpolate, never re-render underneath the user.

layouts.name: masonry
layouts.purpose: Default. The scanning layout; the wall is the product.

layouts.name: stack
layouts.value: full container width, one card per row
layouts.purpose: The reading layout, and the no-JS fallback.

components.name: Note Card
components.description: The signature surface. Identity colour floods the card by day and becomes its edge and glow by night.
components.html:
A slow Saturday

Leave the morning unplanned. Good coffee, the market by the river, then make something with no useful outcome.

Personal2h

narrative.overview:
One desk, photographed twice: mid-morning with the window open, and at midnight with the lamp on. The product does not invert into a dark theme, it changes its light. By day the canvas is warm parchment and notes are soft tinted paper with hairline edges. By night the canvas is a near-black room and each note's colour stops being pigment and becomes a neon edge, chip and glow around it. What makes this one product rather than two is that the skeleton never moves: identical 16px corners, one type system, one spacing rhythm, one motion contract in both themes. The theme toggle should read as dusk falling on a room you already know, not as a different app.

The wall is the product. Notes are scanned, not read one at a time, so colour is an index rather than decoration - a person finds a note again by remembering it was the green one. Density is generous by default because capture is hurried and the feed is glanceable, with a compact mode for people who want more wall at once. The one thing that is never negotiable: neon carries identity, state, chrome and edges, and never running text. Saturated glow behind body copy causes halation, is worst for readers with astigmatism, and fights the colour-blind commitment in PRODUCT.md. Notes get read at length, often in bed.

Confirmed rejections: this is not Keep's corporate Material, and it is not the near-monochrome productivity-tool opposite. It refuses both the pastel-tint-on-white card the category always ships and the neon-on-everything treatment that makes dark themes unreadable.
keyCharacteristics: One skeleton, two lights - geometry, type and motion are theme-invariant
Colour is an index, not decoration; six note identities carry across both themes
Neon is chrome, never running text
Warm neutrals by day (hue ~72-84), cool neutrals by night (hue ~250-265)
Generous by default, compact by choice
Calm motion: overdamped, no bounce, nothing that draws the eye away from text

rules.name: The Neon-Is-Chrome Rule
rules.body: Colour may touch a card's border, chip, glow and edge. It may never touch the title or body text. In the night theme card text is pinned to the neutral inks regardless of the note's identity colour. Audit test: set a card to Hot and screenshot the night theme - if any word of the note changed colour, it is wrong.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Exactly one accent is live at a time and it appears only on chrome: brand mark, active rail item, FAB, focus ring. Accent and note colour are allowed to land on the same hue - they are told apart by placement, never by hue, so never introduce a rule that depends on them differing.

rules.name: The Fallback-Survives Rule
rules.body: Greek, Cyrillic, Japanese and Arabic fall back to the system face, because a covering webfont would cost tens of megabytes. The fallback reads as a different language, not as broken - but it does not carry Bricolage's tight tracking and heavy display weight, so hierarchy must never rest on the display face alone. Size, weight and colour must each carry enough of the difference.

rules.name: The Label Floor Rule
rules.body: Uppercase tracked labels are set at 11px. Do not go below it.

rules.name: The RTL Title Rule
rules.body: Card titles carry dir="auto" so an RTL title flows correctly inside an otherwise LTR card. The card's footer deliberately does not flip, so the wall's controls stay where the rest of the wall put them.

rules.name: The Reading-Order Rule
rules.body: DOM order is always reading order. Any packing algorithm that reorders the DOM to achieve a tighter wall is rejected, however good it looks.

rules.name: The 44px Touch Rule
rules.body: Every interactive control is at least 44x44px in touch mode. The prototype currently fails this everywhere except the FAB - pin is 27px, action buttons are 30px, checklist boxes are 15px.

rules.name: The Glow-Is-Night-Only Rule
rules.body: Glow never appears in the day theme; shadow never carries depth in the night theme. A card that glows on parchment looks like a bug, and a card relying on a drop shadow at midnight looks flat.

rules.name: The Scale-The-Surface-Never-The-Text Rule
rules.body: A hover scale is applied to a dedicated surface layer carrying only background, border, shadow and texture. The content layer never scales. Chrome rasterises text once at its pre-transform size and then bitmap-stretches it, so scaling a layer containing text visibly blurs the card.

rules.name: The Controls-On-Media Rule
rules.body: Any control that can land on top of an attachment needs its own backing - a scrim chip or filled circle - not just a colour. Measured on the current build, 7 of 11 cards place an unbacked pin over media.

rules.name: The Direct-Manipulation Rule
rules.body: Pinning is direct manipulation and must respond on the same frame. Measured on the current build the first frame does not arrive for 115ms, then a 47ms gap, then the card jumps 21px discontinuously before the spring takes over. The cause is a double measure pass in the masonry hook.

rules.name: The Two-Constraint Rule
rules.body: An accent must clear 4.5:1 against its on-accent text AND 3:1 against the canvas behind it. These pull opposite ways in the day theme. The original day amber failed the first (4.27:1); brightening to yellow-amber fixes that (10.24:1) but fails the second at 1.58:1 against parchment, dissolving the button's shape. Night has no tension because the canvas is dark. Resolved day tone oklch(54% 0.15 80): 4.96 on text, 4.55 on canvas.

rules.name: The Pin-Is-Always-In-Front Rule
rules.body: The pin is never occluded, never hover-revealed, never dependent on what is underneath it. It sits above every layer of the card in both layouts and both themes, and carries its own filled backing so it reads against a white photo, a black video thumbnail and a flooded colour card alike.

rules.name: The Two-Layouts Rule
rules.body: Masonry and Stack are the complete set. No third feed mode, and neither may grow its own card variant.

rules.name: The Layout-Switch Is Animated Rule
rules.body: Switching between Masonry and Stack animates; every card travels from its old slot to its new one. Both layouts resolve to per-card x/y/width targets through the same placement path, so the switch is a change of target rather than a change of rendering strategy.

dos: Do keep the skeleton theme-invariant: 16px corners, one type scale, one spacing rhythm, one motion contract. Only the light changes.
Do let the note's identity colour drive the card's border, chip and glow, and stop there.
Do hold the accent hue steady across themes and change only its lightness, so the toggle reads as dusk.
Do scale a dedicated surface layer on hover and never the layer holding text.
Do pair every motion affordance with a material change, so reduced motion still communicates state.
Do give every control that can land on media its own backing.
Do keep DOM order equal to reading order in the packed wall.
Do hold metadata labels at 11px (0.6875rem) or larger.
Do measure a new accent four ways - against its on-accent text (4.5:1) and against its canvas (3:1), in both themes.
Do keep the pin above every other layer of the card, with its own filled backing, in both layouts and both themes.
Do animate the Masonry-to-Stack switch, resolving both layouts through the same placement path so they can interpolate.
Do fill the FAB with the accent; a shadow is depth, not a shape.
donts: Don't put neon, glow or any saturated identity colour behind or on running text. This is the system's single hardest rule.
Don't let the accent appear anywhere but chrome - brand mark, active rail item, FAB, focus ring.
Don't write a rule that depends on the accent and a note colour being different hues; they are told apart by placement.
Don't use glow in the day theme or rely on drop shadow for depth in the night theme.
Don't spend horizontal space on card chrome - it is the scarce axis on a phone.
Don't introduce a second border weight or a dashed border to signal an incomplete chip; differ by fill.
Don't ship a touch target under 44x44px.
Don't let a hover-revealed control be the only way to reach an action, because on touch it does not exist.
Don't add a webfont to cover Greek, Cyrillic, CJK or Arabic; fall back to the system face and make sure hierarchy survives without the display face.
Don't let the wall overshoot or bounce when it re-packs.
Don't brighten the day accent to fix its text contrast - it dissolves into the parchment canvas. Day is deep, night is bright, because the canvas is inverted.
Don't add a third feed layout, or let Masonry and Stack grow separate card variants.
Don't render Stack through a different code path than Masonry; a layout that renders differently cannot animate into one that doesn't.
